markdown_empty: Your rendered markdown will appear here.
markdown_sample_intro:
Type **Markdown** on the left and watch it render live on the right.
Everything runs on your device. Nothing is uploaded.

cron_header_desc: Choose how often a job runs, read the schedule in plain English and check when it runs next. Everything happens on your device.
cron_fix_expression: Fix the expression to see when it runs.
cron_never_runs: This schedule never runs. A date like 31 February does not exist.
cron_sym_comma_example: 1,15 in day of month means the 1st and 15th
cron_sym_dash_example: 1-5 in day of week means Monday to Friday
cron_hint_default: Five fields: minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week.
cron_either_note: When both day of month and day of week are set, the job runs on either one. Shortcuts like @daily and @hourly also work.
cron_week_min_one: A weekly schedule keeps at least one day.
cron_dom_label: On which day of the month?
cron_dom_skip: Months with fewer days are skipped.
cron_builder_cannot: The builder cannot show this schedule. Pick how often to replace it, or keep editing it as text.
cron_minute_legend: At which minute of the hour?
cron_err_out_of_range: {text} is outside {min} to {max} for the {field} field.
cron_err_not_number_or_name: "{text}" is not a number or a {field} name.
cron_err_not_number: "{text}" is not a number. The {field} field takes {min} to {max}.
cron_err_empty_entry: There is an empty entry in a list.
cron_err_bad_step: The step in "{text}" must be a whole number of 1 or more.
cron_err_backwards: The range "{text}" runs backwards. Put the smaller value first.
cron_err_reboot: @reboot runs at startup, so it has no schedule to show.
cron_err_six_fields: This tool reads five fields. Drop the seconds field and try again.
cron_err_seven_fields: This tool reads five fields. Drop the seconds and year field and try again.
cron_err_field_count: A cron expression has five fields, and this one has {count}.
